instructions: Coarsely grate the Gruyère. That should be about 1 1/2 cups. Finely grate 1/2 cup parmesan. Put 1 cup of the Gruyère and all the parmesan in a bowl and toss them together. Keep the other 1/2 cup Gruyère for the sauce.
Melt 2 tbsp of the butter in a small saucepan over medium. Whisk in the 2 tbsp flour and cook it for 1 minute, whisking, until it bubbles and smells a little toasty.

Pour in the 1 1/3 cups milk a little at a time, whisking all the while so no lumps form. Drop in the bay leaf and let it bubble gently for 2 to 3 minutes, whisking, until it's thick enough to coat a spoon.
Take it off the heat and fish out the bay leaf. Whisk in the 1/2 cup Gruyère you kept, the 2 tsp Dijon, the nutmeg and a pinch each of salt and pepper until it's smooth.
Turn the broiler on high with a rack about 6 inches below it, and line a baking sheet with foil.

Cut 8 slices of the sourdough. Melt 1 tbsp butter in a large skillet over medium high and toast 4 slices on one side only, until golden, about 2 minutes. Repeat with 1 more tbsp butter and the other 4 slices.
Lay all 8 slices on the sheet with the untoasted side up and spread a spoonful of the sauce on each one. Put 2 slices of ham and a small handful of the cheese mix on 4 of them.
Close each sandwich with a plain slice, toasted side up. Spread the rest of the sauce over the tops and scatter on the rest of the cheese mix.
Broil for 3 to 4 minutes, until the cheese is bubbling and browned in spots. Watch them closely. They go from golden to burnt fast.

While they broil, melt the last 1 tbsp butter in a large nonstick skillet over medium. Crack in the 4 eggs, add a pinch of salt and cook for 3 to 4 minutes, until the whites are firm and the yolks are still runny.
Slide an egg onto each sandwich and serve straight away.
method_notes: All three make a Mornay, a béchamel with Gruyère melted in, layer ham and more Gruyère in the bread, cover the top with the sauce and cheese, broil until bubbling and finish with a fried egg with a runny yolk. The Jam Jar Kitchen toasts the bread on one side only, flavors the sauce with a bay leaf, Dijon and nutmeg, and mixes parmesan into the cheese for the top. Sweet Tea and Thyme browns the whole sandwich in a skillet before saucing and broiling, and covers the eggs as they fry. Taste of Home spreads sauce inside the sandwich too, with mustard optional, and grills it in butter before broiling.
